newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Six newspapers shut down in Liberia over permits.
newsitem.headline: Six newspapers shut down in Liberia over permits.

text.p: The interim government in Liberia shut down six leading newspapers on Tuesday, saying they had failed to renew their 1997 permits.
One of the dailes named by Information Minister Joe Mulbah is The Patriot, owned by Liberia's former chief warlord Charles Taylor, now a leading presidential contender.
The others are the National, owned by Taylor's rival warlord and fellow presidential hopeful Alhaji Kromah, the Daily News, The Heritage, Chronicles and The News.
"These papers will not operate until they meet the guidelines promulgated by the ministry of information," said Mulbah, a Taylor appointee in the coalition government.
There was no immediate comment from the newspapers.
Liberia is preparing for elections on May 30 to wrap up a regional peace process after seven years of civil war.
